newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Nat.Grid yr profits rise, costs cut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nat.Grid yr profits rise, costs cut.

text.p: British electricity transmission network operator National Grid Group Plc turned in annual profits within expectations on Tuesday and confirmed cost cuts to offset partly a price review agreed last October.

The company said pretax profits for the year ending March 31 were 591.4 million pounds ($966.5 million), within expectations and up 12.2 percent from pro forma results a year ago to take account of its flotation in December 1995.
It paid out a dividend of 11.13 pence per share and finance director John Uttley said it expected to show growth of four to five percent in real terms in its payout for the next four years.

"We have made rapid progress on rationalising transmission which will enable us to cut controllable costs aggressively and offset, as far as we are able, the effects of the new price control," the company said in a statement.
Uttley told Reuters that National Grid expected the cuts to be over 10 percent in the current year but to average six percent a year over the next four years.

National Grid agreed a price review with regulator Offer last October which included a one-off cut of 20 percent in the current year and said in November it expected to cut costs by around six percent a year with 750 job losses likely.
Shares in the company were hardly changed on Tuesday, down half a penny at 225 pence by 0920 GMT.

The company said it was "encouraged" by the "significant progress" of its telecommunications unit Energis, as turnover jumped 127 percent to 97.1 million pounds and operating losses shrank 26 percent to 54.2 million.
"The business is growing very well indeed," Uttley said.
He told Reuters that the company felt Energis had grown to such a size that a single partnership deal was "not likely to be the issue."
"Whereas 18 months, two years ago, looking for a single big partner seemed to be the right way to go, we now think it's unlikely that will be the way ahead," he said.
The company later clarified that it was not ruling out the possibility of such a deal but that the growth in Energis broadened its options.
Energis had said in January that National Grid might sell a stake in the company, possibly going below 50 percent for one or more strategic investors.
Uttley said it was "quite possible that equity deals could be on the agenda in the right circumstances but...the present thrust is developing the business."

National Grid had made representations to the new Labour government over its proposed one-off tax on "excess profits" of privatised utilities which will be used to finance a three billion pound programme to cut unemployment, Uttley said.

He said National Grid had argued that its ownership by the regional electricity companies (Recs) until demerger in December 1995 and a 50 pound customer rebate made it different from other companies under scrutiny for the tax.
Labour, which stormed to victory in a landslide general election win on May 1, has vowed to introduce the tax at its first budget, scheduled for July 2.

Internationally, Uttley said National Grid was "very happy" with returns from its operations in Argentina, with rates of return "in the teens," adding that National Grid felt it could improve on that "a little."
Uttley said National Grid was looking at projects in India, Zambia and Australia as well as its interests in Argentina.

The company is suing Pakistan's government for cancelling an overhead power lines project while in Kazakhstan, National Grid dropped negotiations over a contract although Uttley said it remains in touch with authorities there.
"It's a long haul overseas. (Projects) do not come quickly," he said. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
